text.title: Quit Day Job Trigger Contract Worked Example
text.summary: One complete contract for a solo SaaS builder on Stripe (net MRR at 4,000 USD for 3 month-ends, runway floor 12 months from 40,600 savings over a 3,100 burn, gates at 20 percent and 5 percent, reversal at 3,000 for 2 month-ends, committed 2026-02-01, two quarterly reviews ending in a fired verdict on readings of 4,150, 4,300 and 4,420) with a note per value, plus a post-hoc gross-cash contract and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A solo builder runs a SaaS on Stripe Billing while employed. In February 2026, with net MRR at 3,200 USD, they write the contract: 4,000 USD for three consecutive month-ends, 12 months of runway, no customer above 20 percent, gross churn under 5 percent, reversal at 3,000 for two month-ends. The June review shows readings of 3,480, 3,720 and 3,910; the September review shows 4,150, 4,300 and 4,420 with 13.1 months of runway, the top customer at 11 percent and churn at 2.8 percent.

example.title: Stripe net MRR contract, fired at the September 2026 review
example.note: The metric is Stripe Billing's net MRR report, so annual plans, refunds and one-time fees cannot inflate a reading (r-mrr-definition-pinned). Three consecutive month-ends at or above 4,000 are required; the June review's 3,480, 3,720, 3,910 leave the count at zero (r-consecutive-months-window). Savings of 40,600 over a 3,100 burn that includes self-employment tax, health insurance and business costs is 13.1 months, above the floor of 12, computed on 2026-08-31 (r-runway-co-condition). The reversal at 3,000 for two month-ends sits 1,000 below the trigger, so a bad month cannot flip the decision back inside a quarter (r-reversal-hysteresis). No customer above 20 percent and churn under 5 percent are stated as fractions and both hold in September at 0.11 and 0.028 (r-concentration-and-churn-gate). Version 1.0.0 was committed on 2026-02-01, four months before the first qualifying reading of 2026-06-30, so post_hoc is false and the change log holds one entry (r-precommit-before-threshold). Both evidence links resolve to the Stripe MRR report and the runway model file and name the month-end they cover (r-evidence-is-provider-export). The conclusion names the action, the first-of-the-month date rule, 30 days notice and the order partner, manager, customers (r-conclusion-is-dated-action). Each review entry carries its readings, runway, gate values and a verdict; last_run_at is the September entry, whose three qualifying readings with runway and gates satisfied make the verdict fired (r-quarterly-review-records-readings).

example.title: a post-hoc gross-cash contract
example.note: What the validator prints: `trigger.metric` must be net_mrr, `provider` spreadsheet is not a named provider, `consecutive_month_ends` 1 below 3 (r-mrr-definition-pinned, r-consecutive-months-window); `burn_includes` lacks self_employment_tax, health_insurance and business_costs (r-runway-co-condition); `reversal.consecutive_month_ends` 1 below 2 and `runway_below_months` 0 not above 0 (r-reversal-hysteresis); `conclusion.statement` matches "when ready" and is too short, `date_rule` too short, `inform_order` empty, the evidence link is a screenshot with a kind outside the enum (r-conclusion-is-dated-action, r-evidence-is-provider-export); the review entry has 0 readings (r-quarterly-review-records-readings). Once the schema violations are fixed the cross-field checks add: reversal 4,000 is not below trigger 4,000; the contract was committed on 2026-07-03, after a qualifying month-end, without post_hoc; and a fired verdict with no qualifying readings while the top customer is 71 percent and churn 9 percent.
